checked: OSU/Kappler p. 398 prints two June 18, 1833 relinquishments: Mulatto King and Tustenuggy Hajo (7 Stat. 427, proclaimed Apr. 12, 1834) and Econchatimico (7 Stat. 428).

Royce schedule (1823 and 1833 rows): one cession 'with the Appalachicola band' (Yellow Hare's improvements, Mulatto King) and a separate one 'with certain chiefs in Florida' (Econchatimico's Chattahoochee reserve). treaties.json maps kappler-406/area 184 to the Appalachicola band and kappler-407/area 185 to certain chiefs in Florida.
Econchatimico text: three sections by patent within three years; annuity share; $3,000 if they join the Seminoles west.
Patents question: no court, ICC or government finding located; ExploreSouthernHistory (historian) says Econchatimico received the $3,000 in October 1838 and went west under escort.
